title: Search for stable hadronising squarks and gluinos with the ATLAS experiment at the LHC
extended_summary:
This paper is a particle-physics search for stable hadronising squarks and gluinos (R-hadrons) using the ATLAS detector at the LHC, not a study in education. The analysis asks whether slow-moving, long-lived, coloured supersymmetric particles can be detected in proton-proton collisions at 7 TeV by combining measurements of ionisation energy loss in the pixel detector and time-of-flight in the tile calorimeter.

The approach uses 34 pb−1 of ATLAS collision data, together with Monte Carlo simulation and a data-driven background estimate, to reconstruct candidate masses and define signal regions for several mass hypotheses. The work examines multiple interaction models for R-hadrons in matter and studies systematic uncertainties from theory, detector response, and background estimation.

No evidence for signal is found. The paper sets 95% confidence-level lower mass limits for stable sbottoms, stops, and gluinos, with the most conservative limits reported as 294 GeV, 309 GeV, and 562 GeV respectively. Since the paper is entirely about high-energy physics and contains no education-related intervention, population, or user data, the education fields are not reported.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a high-energy physics paper about ATLAS searches for long-lived hadronising squarks and gluinos, not an education study. It does not evaluate any educational technology, AI intervention, or learner outcome relevant to the requested taxonomy.
impact_tier_rationale: There is no educational intervention or student outcome assessed, so there is no impact on middle school mathematics achievement or any K-12 education outcome.
